## Historical audit: S0283

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/test/bw_0056/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file. The supplied observations are whole lines; no split offsets are needed.

**Goal versus evidence:** The assigned goal was to reconstruct a single indoor photograph with editable meshes and matching camera, framing, placement and materials (line 1, `model_request`). The scene description below is the student’s interpretation, not an independent inspection of the reference.

| Stage | Observed evidence |
|---|---|
| Initial construction | H inventoried a cleanroom, two workers, a packaging machine, conveyor, guard and articulated screen, then emitted separate named parts for them. Code specified translucent guard panels, metallic/roughness settings, a posed reaching arm, camera, world and lights (lines 3–4, `model_response` and `execute`). Names and hierarchy establish emitted parts, not correct object identification, physical connection or reference fidelity. |
| First validation and revision | Build and render completed with return code 0; `execution_result` was `ok: true` and recorded a saved image (lines 6, 8–9). The next request supplied that render to H (line 11). H reported a distant scene, excess floor, intrusive wall and small screen; it moved the camera closer, changed the screen proportions, rounded the operator and strengthened dark machinery (lines 13–14). These are H’s visual judgments and executed changes, not independently verified defects or improvements. |
| Second revision | The second build and render also succeeded (lines 16, 18–19). After receiving its image (line 21), H reported small, low people, a misplaced upright screen, weak dark layering and an open background edge. Its third program enlarged/repositioned figures, moved and tilted the screen, added a wall and dark panel, and changed camera and lighting settings (lines 23–24). H’s intended hand-to-screen contact and articulated support remain geometrically unverified. |
| Final outcome | Step 3 built and rendered successfully and was selected (lines 26, 28–30). This is **technical execution success**, not established visual correctness or formal task success. No final image review or `DONE` response is recorded; no independent assessment of the final pose, contacts, material appearance, texture, framing or lighting is available. |

**Teacher and exploration:** No teacher message, teacher diagnosis, proposed update, or evidence of student receipt or adoption appears in this student trajectory. The revisions are H’s own responses to runner-provided render feedback. Sessions reported zero observable tool calls, with tools disabled; iterative program generation and runner executions are visible, but other autonomous tool exploration is not (lines 2, 12, 22).

**Lessons and uncertainty:** Transferably, a successful build and render validate execution, not the image match; recording a comparison before a revision makes the causal intent auditable. The closer camera, taller display and dark panel are scene-specific hypotheses, not generally validated fixes. The reference and rendered pixels are not supplied to this audit, so whether multiple objects are correctly represented, whether parts actually meet, and whether the revisions improved fidelity remain unresolved.
